The Catcher in the Rye

Chapter 1

If you really want to hear about it, the first thing you'll probably want to know is where I was born.
And what my lousy childhood was like, and how my parents were occupied and all before they had me.
And all that David Copperfield kind of crap.
But I don't feel like going into it, if you want to know the truth.
In the first place, that stuff bores me.
And in the second place, my parents would have about two hemorrhages apiece if I told anything pretty personal about them.

Chapter 2 — Departure

The day I left Pencey, it was snowing like a son of a bitch.
I came down from Thomsen Hill that afternoon.
The wind on the hill made my face hurt, but I didn't turn back.
I stood at the top of the hill and looked at Pencey for the last time.
Then I turned around and left.

Chapter 3 - On the Train

Ten minutes after the train left Pencey, I started thinking about Jane.
I thought about her profile, and how she always paused before speaking.
I didn't finish the book, but I would miss her.
Sometimes you don't forget someone — sometimes the opposite happens.
